title: Keyboard Manager caps lock still activates sometimes

fix_assessment.rationale: An observable failure is reported and a specific investigation boundary is identified. The proposed direction remains conditional on controlled reproduction.

steps: Use a disposable session with test text and CapsLock to Esc; record toggle state on the normal desktop.
Open a standard UAC prompt, press CapsLock, dismiss the prompt normally and compare toggle/remap state after return; do not attempt to hook the secure desktop.
Separately repeat ordinary-app held-key/focus transitions without UAC; distinguish protected-desktop toggle changes from hook loss or injection failure before designing recovery.
prerequisites: Use a disposable test environment and test-owned documents/configuration; preserve existing user data.
reproduce.expected: Protected-desktop limitations must remain intact. Returning to the normal desktop should have a clearly understood, recoverable toggle/remap state, and ordinary-desktop failures need their own regression rather than a blanket elevation workaround.

actions.label: Reproduce Keyboard Manager Caps Lock transitions behavior

evidence: The long thread includes different mappings, supplied archives, elevated/non-elevated contrasts and independent ordinary-app reports; these do not all establish one cause.
The latest precise reproduction toggles Caps Lock during a Windows UAC prompt while CapsLock is mapped to Esc.

Official documentation says Keyboard Manager does not run on password/Run As Admin screens. Earlier reports also describe failures outside that protected context, including while PowerToys is already elevated.
judgment.rationale: A protected-desktop keypress can change the OS Caps Lock toggle while the normal-desktop hook cannot intercept it; returning to a remapped key then makes toggling it back awkward. Investigate transition/state reconciliation separately from ordinary-desktop hook or injection failures; never propose intercepting the secure desktop or claim elevation universally fixes the issue.
judgment.recommended_action: Execute the focused maintainer reproduction before choosing an implementation; the proposal is a hypothesis, not an approved detailed design.

verification: Protected-desktop limitations must remain intact. Returning to the normal desktop should have a clearly understood, recoverable toggle/remap state, and ordinary-desktop failures need their own regression rather than a blanket elevation workaround.
Retest a matching unaffected control and the originally reported workflow on a current supported build.
